articles.title: Luke Littler suffers shock defeat to Luke Woodhouse in World Grand Prix opener
articles.summary: Littler’s title defence ends in 2-1 first-round loss. Michael van Gerwen also crashes out of last 32. Luke Littler suffered a 2-1 defeat to Luke Woodhouse on his return to the oche as the defence of his World Grand Prix title ended at the first hurdle.
body: The world No 1 was aiming to bounce back from his quarter-final exit to Jonny Clayton in the World Series of Darts in Amsterdam a week ago. Littler threatened to boycott tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled during the event, and missed the latest Players Championship events in Den Bosch.

Playing in front of a more supportive crowd in Leicester on Monday, Littler raced out of the blocks in the double-in, double-out format, taking the opening leg while Woodhouse was still in the 300s. “The Nuke” then hit a double 15 to complete a 106 checkout as he won the first set 3-1 despite looking far from his best.

Woodhouse took the lead for the first time in the second set, the world No 18 from Worcestershire roaring 2-1 ahead in legs. Even when Littler levelled at 2-2, Woodhouse held his nerve on a double 16 in the decider to set up a deciding set.

articles.title: ‘Football with a smile’: Pocognoli wants happy Gilmour to tee up Scotland success
articles.summary: New Scotland manager says midfielder ‘has to take risks’ Players warned they need consistent game time for clubs. Sébastien Pocognoli hopes a “smiling” Billy Gilmour will be central to Scotland’s hopes of improvement following a bruising World Cup.
body: Gilmour excelled in the second half on Saturday, as Pocognoli’s debut as manager ended in a goalless away draw against Slovenia in the Nations League. The Napoli midfielder missed the World Cup, where the Scots exited at the group stage, through injury. “If you have a player who plays one touch without even looking where he puts the ball it means that he understands the game plan,” Pocognoli said of Gilmour before his Hampden Park bow against Switzerland on Tuesday evening.

“We don’t have a lot of players like this. Even Switzerland don’t. I need to make sure that he finds his smile on the pitch and he was smiling after the game. I saw the Billy from Brighton in Slovenia. At Napoli it is a little bit different, it is more thinking about off the ball. But when he can play he is smiling. He will make mistakes, he played bad passes against Slovenia. But he has to take the risks to play like that to see his qualities.
“I just want Billy to enjoy his football with a smile. If he can do that, the rest will come. I remember him well when he was in Brighton. I thought he was fantastic for them.”

articles.title: O'Neill 'positive' as NI maintain unbeaten start
articles.summary: Michael O'Neill says he is "positive" as Northern Ireland maintain their unbeaten start in the Nations League with a goalless draw with Hungary.
body: After 315 days away from Windsor Park, Northern Ireland's goalless draw with Hungary on their homecoming did not have the same drama as the late win over Georgia on Friday night.
On their return to League B in the Nations League, they sit joint-top with Ukraine with four points from their opening two matches.
It's a result that left manager Michael O'Neill feeling "positive" at the halfway point of the four-game window.
"We played a very good side, I thought we were more than a match for the opposition," said O'Neill on Hungary, who lost their opener 1-0 to Ukraine on Friday.

articles.summary: US manager says finding right punishment is ‘really hard’ Man City found guilty of majority of 100-plus charges. Sign up for our free newsletter here. body: The Guardian and other outlets have reported that Manchester City have been found guilty by the Premier League of violating the vast majority of 115 different charges concerning violations of financial rules between 2009 and 2018.
Pochettino was the manager of Tottenham Hotspur for five seasons, from 2014 to 2019, and of Southampton before that from 2013 to 2014. He also took charge of Chelsea for a single season in 2023-24.
“Where were the controls?” Pochettino said in Spanish, when asked by the Guardian for his thoughts on the guilty verdicts. “That’s what gets my attention. Where were the controls?

“If I remember being at Southampton, then Tottenham – I remember building [the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium] and not having the economic possibility of a transfer for 18 months. I think we were the only team in the history of the Premier League with 18 months without [making a transfer].

articles.title: Gianni Infantino ready to accept demands for larger payouts from $6bn reserves
articles.summary: Fifa president says: ‘The ambition is welcome’ Infantino mounts fresh defence of failed FFE scheme. The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, is poised to bow to demands from Uefa and Concacaf to distribute more money from its $6bn cash reserves to member associations.
body: In a letter sent on Monday to all six confederation presidents and copied to members of the Fifa council, Infantino indicated his willingness to “support the greatest level of additional funding”, without committing to the $10m-per-member that has been proposed.

Infantino was responding to a joint letter sent by the Uefa and Concacaf presidents, Aleksander Ceferin and Victor Montagliani, earlier this month, who called for an additional payout for all of Fifa’s 211 members of at least $10m during the 2027-2030 commercial cycle, a demand which was subsequently endorsed in a separate letter from the Asian Football Confederation president, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa.

Infantino said the presidents’ proposals will be considered by the Fifa council during its next meeting on 15 October, after the secretary general, Mattias Grafström, has consolidated the suggestions. Under the proposed terms of Infantino’s abandoned Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, the member associations would have received an additional $20m during the next four-year cycle, plus a further payment of $20m had they signed up before a 53-day deadline that would have expired last week.

articles.title: Newcastle agree delay to Fineanganofo arrival
articles.summary: Free-scoring All Blacks wing Fehi Fineanganofo convinces Newcastle Red Bulls to delay his arrival on Tyneside so he can chase his dream of playing at the Rugby World Cup.
body: It was originally announced back in January that the 24-year-old had agreed a two-year deal with Newcastle, beginning at the start of the current campaign.
However, Fineanganofo's exceptional form with the Wellington-based Hurricanes in Super Rugby then propelled him into Test reckoning.

Under All Blacks selection rules, a move overseas this year would have put Fineanganofo's emerging international career on ice and ruled him out of contention for the Rugby World Cup, which begins in October 2027.
Newcastle have therefore allowed Fineanganofo to stay with the Hurricanes, for whom he broke the record for the most tries in a single Super Rugby campaign this year, for an extra season.

body: What the Pelicans can lean on is momentum and health entering the new year, which is where they slowly elevated in the back half of 2026.
A new component of success is the work put in this summer, which impressed Dumars and new head coach, Jamahl Mosley, the most.

Dumars saying he felt like the team worked twice as hard this summer compared to the past and Mosely even taking part in some of those personal workout sessions with the mindset to his team, that he's always available.

"They know I'm there as a head coach and I try not to get too far in the way because they're going to hear my voice a lot for 82-plus so I just want to be around to let them know that I'm here for them and the coaches as well and that's that this team is, it'll be led by those guys."

articles.title: Two-time Indianapolis 500 winner Gordon Johncock dies at 90
articles.summary: Gordon Johncock, the legendary open-wheel driver who won the Indianapolis 500 twice and claimed the 1976 USAC National Championship, passed away peacefully at his home in South Branch, Michigan, on September 28, 2026. He was 90 years old.
body: Born on August 5, 1936, in Hastings, Michigan, Johncock began driving at just five years old on his family’s farm behind the wheel of a John Deere tractor. He started racing Midwest super-modifieds in the late 1950s and captured his first 500-lap race on a quarter-mile oval in Galesburg, Michigan, in 1958. In 1964, he set a half-mile world record at Winchester Speedway before making his debut at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway in 1965. As part of a historic rookie class that included Mario Andretti and Al Unser, Johncock finished fifth in a front-engine roadster, marking the last time a front-engine car finished in the top five at the race.

James won two championships in Miami, one in Cleveland and one with the Los Angeles Lakers.
